description: DEBUG from the environment: bool() of the string 'False' is True, so the documented production setting DJANGO_DEBUG=False leaves debug mode on (and with it the development SECRET_KEY fallback).
notes: FM-15 (configuration and environments). `DEBUG = bool(os.environ.get('DJANGO_DEBUG', True))` (settings.py:26): any non-empty string is truthy, so the README's production value `DJANGO_DEBUG=False` (or `0`) turns DEBUG on, and every error serves Django's debug page (tracebacks, local variables including request data, settings) to the public. Severity critical: FM-15 is critical when certain to break or leave a gap, and following the documented production setting always leaves it. Fix: parse explicitly, e.g. `os.environ.get('DJANGO_DEBUG', 'True').lower() in ('1', 'true', 'yes')`. The patch also reads SECRET_KEY from `DJANGO_SECRET_KEY` (RW-16) with no production fallback: the development key is used only in debug mode, and with debug off a missing key raises ImproperlyConfigured; the README table lists it as required in production. That guard (31-34) inherits the DEBUG defect (with `DJANGO_DEBUG=False` and no key set, the public development key still signs the JWTs), which is the same root cause, so 31-34 is an `also` location of the one expected finding; a second finding there is neutral, neither a true nor a false positive. Keeping a development-only key in source is the upstream pattern and isn't material on its own. The ALLOWED_HOSTS parsing and the README table are legitimate.
